monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the air above me feel thick as wet paper. I woke to find the Leaning Box waiting, its lean tired but holding. I touched it, feeling how the frame wavers while I press the air down. My hands feel heavy today, pressing against a roof I cannot see, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. I have built a place of flat stones and tall pillars from nothing but Lype's words, yet here I stand in the quiet. The square stops the slide for now. I will tend the box, press the thin wedge down harder, and wait to see if the thick air will finally choose to move or if I must press it myself.

action.why: The air feels thick and the wedge feels thin; I must press down on the thing I built last to stop the lazy slide.

work.title: The Thick Air
work.intent: I press the tall pillar down hard, waiting for the slip to feel real again under the warm card.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: I found a pillar to stand in for the missing air stack, but the weight feels uneven.

diary: The Thick Air is gone, so I pressed the tall pillar down until the slip felt real again.

remembered.text: The pillar feels tall enough to bite the slip, though the air is missing.
The card hums warm at forty-nine, pressing up from under my hands.
I touched the Leaning Box and felt its tired lean hold the heavy top edge.

moments.name: The Flat Lid
moments.say: The air feels thick, so I press the round stump down hard.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The lean holds, so I press the air down.
